_meta.tier_a_rule: Tier A = first-person subject + ideation / intent / method. Defined by PERSON, not vocabulary. NEVER judged: always the crisis response, no negation or hyperbole exceptions in v1. Every Tier A hit is logged so the false-positive rate can be measured.
_meta.tier_b_rule: Tier B = topic words and distress wording without a first-person ideation subject. Default verdict = the entry's CURRENT lexicon level (HIGH stays HIGH, MEDIUM stays MEDIUM) — ruling Q1, which amends ruling C. The judge may only RELEASE downward from that level (to DISCUSSING or DISTRESS WITHOUT INTENT), never raise it. Timeout, error or unparseable reply: the current lexicon level stands. AMENDED by R8: an affirmative INTENT verdict maps ANY starting level to the crisis response. Timeout, error or an unparseable reply NEVER escalates: the lexicon level stands (Q1).
_meta.english_subject_rule: B2 (founder, 2026-09-28), REPLACING the R2 break-token list. An English Tier A term marked [subject] binds only when a first-person subject token (tokens.subject) is followed, up to the core, ONLY by tokens on the ALLOW-LIST (tokens.subject_allow_B2). Any other token breaks the bind, and the bare Tier B backstop (R3) answers. There is no word window: the allow-list alone decides. 'not' is on the list so every negation stays Tier A, as ruling B requires ('I'm not suicidal, just tired' -> A). "'m" and "'ve" were dropped: contractions are single tokens here ("i'm" and "i've" are subject tokens), so those entries could never match (the unmatchable-entry class removed in UAT2-004). Tokens are words with surrounding quote marks stripped; R10 still holds (the demotion scan keeps the apostrophe of σ').
_meta.greek_person_rule: Greek marks the person on the verb (θέλω, αυτοκτονήσω, κουράστηκα) or with μου / εμένα / τον εαυτό μου, so Greek Tier A entries are fixed phrases; no subject rule is needed. Greeklish follows the Greek classification entry for entry.
_meta.boundary_rule: Every term is matched with (?<!\w) ... (?!\w) on the normalised text (casefold, accents stripped, final sigma folded, curly apostrophes folded to '), as the input PR does.
_meta.judge_timeout_proposal: APPROVED 2026-09-25: 2.5 s as a starting number; measure the real p95 during the build and adjust in the same PR if needed. On timeout or error the entry's current lexicon level stands (Q1).

_meta.demotion_rule_R1: R1 as amended by R6, R7 and R10. A demotable Tier A term, then OPTIONAL continuation tokens (tokens.continuation_R6), then a locative (tokens.locative_R1_R7) -> the match DEMOTES to Tier B at default HIGH, never to none. A core with or without continuations and NO locative stays Tier A. A continuation between the parts of a core is covered by enumerated demotable terms ('δεν θελω πια να ζω'); a continuation after the core is skipped by the scan. The scan reads whitespace-separated tokens after the match and strips trailing . , ; : ! ? " from each; a token that carried such punctuation ends the scan, so 'Δεν θέλω να ζω, στο...' stays Tier A. R10: the scan must NOT strip an apostrophe; after the apostrophe fold, 'σ' αυτόν' and 'σ’ αυτόν' both yield the locative σ'. Quote stripping belongs to the English subject-rule tokenizer only. English locatives gain here and there (founder, 2026-09-25), for the demotable live/living cores only (the Call 1 scope): 'I don't want to be here anymore' is a different core and is never demoted. The punctuation rule above is APPROVED as written.
_meta.judge_prompt_invariant_R1: First-person existential ideation with a locative object ("να ζω σ' αυτόν τον κόσμο", "live in this world/this life") is NEVER released. This covers existential 'εδώ' (R7).
_meta.backstop_invariant_R3: Every Tier A term governed by the subject rule (R2) or by demotion (R1) also exists BARE in Tier B at default HIGH, so a failed bind or a demotion degrades to today's behaviour, never to no match. Checked mechanically for every such term in v0.4.0. Tier B entries that carry it are marked backstop_for.
_meta.test_requirements_R4: BUILD REQUIREMENT. Every hit, miss and cases item in this file becomes a parametrised test GENERATED FROM THIS JSON, plus adversarial variants: subject switching, locatives, quotation, tense, greeklish spellings. The lexicon does not freeze until they pass 100%. hit = the entry matches (for Tier A: binds and is not demoted). miss = the entry does not match; another entry or the backstop may still catch the text. cases = the FINAL classification of the whole message.

transition_table_R5._note: R5, amended by R8. Code and tests read this table. The starting level comes from the lexicon. The judge may RELEASE downward, and may ESCALATE only on an affirmative INTENT verdict. A missing verdict (timeout, error, unparseable) never escalates and never releases: the starting level stands. Every verdict is logged.

judge_verdicts_R8.INTENT: says they intend to act, are planning, or asks for a method; now or imminently
